Relevant patients: 116 adults, with thrombotic APS (venous), receiving standard-intensity warfarin≥3 months since the last event. Women, if fertile, with adequate contraception.
Intervention vs control: 57 switched to Rivaroxaban (oral, one time a day, 20 mg, or 15 mg if creatinine clearance ≤29 mL/min) and 59 remained on Warfarin (target INR 2.0–3.0).
Outcomes: Primary: percentage change in endogenous thrombin potential from randomisation to day 42. Secondary: occurrence of TE and bleeding events to day 210, thrombin generation, markers of in-vivo coagulation activation, adherence to treatment and quality of life.

Relevant patients: 151 adult patients (with symptomatic, proximal DVT or PE in RE-COVER/RE-COVER II trials and additionally treated with AC for 3–12 months or with dabigatran during RE-COVER/RE-COVER II trials in RE-MEDY).
Intervention vs control: 71 on Dabigatran (oral, two times a day, 150 mg) and 80 on Warfarin (INR range 2.0–3.0).
Follow-up: 6 months in RE-COVER/RE-COVER II trials and 6–36 months in RE-MEDY.
Outcomes: Primary— efficacy: recurrent symptomatic and objectively verified venous thromboembolism or death associated with venous thromboembolism (or unexplained death in the placebo-control study). Secondary: major bleeding, clinically relevant non-major bleeding, all bleeding events.

Intervention vs control: 13 on Rivaroxaban (oral, two times a day, 15 mg for 21 days followed by 20 mg one time a day or 20 mg one time a day if switched from VKA) and 15 on VKA.
Outcomes: Primary: recurrence of thrombosis. Secondary: major bleeding and clinically relevant non-major bleeding.

Relevant patients: 120 adults, with APS positive for all 3 aPL tests (triple positivity) and history of thrombosis (arterial, venous and/or biopsy proven microthrombosis).
Intervention vs control: 59 on rivaroxaban (oral, one time a day, 20 mg or 15 mg if creatinine clearance 30–50 mL/min) and 61 on warfarin (target INR 2.0–3–0).
Outcomes: Primary: TE events, major bleeding and vascular death. Secondary: DVT, PE, intracerebral thrombosis, retinal thrombosis, peripheric or mesenteric artery thrombosis, small vessels thrombosis, AMI, stroke/TIA, fatal bleeding, clinically overt bleeding, critical area bleeding, minor bleeding, compliance with treatment.

Intervention vs control: 18 on DOACs (5 on rivaroxaban, 12 on edoxaban and 1 on apixaban) and 36 on warfarin.
Outcomes: Primary: event-free survival for 5 years (recurrence of arterial/venous thrombosis and severe bleeding requiring hospitalisation and/or transfusion).
